extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH PHS 398-style biomedical grant applications (PIs and key personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required-format elements for preparing a PHS 398 research grant application (biographical sketches, facilities/resources, specific aims, background/significance, and research support listings) aimed at biomedical researchers applying for NIH-style funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketch format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the key personnel in the order listed for Form Page 2. Follow the sample format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include NAME and POSITION TITLE. Provide sections A (Positions and Honors), B (Selected peer-reviewed publications in chronological order), and C (Research Support). Use the sample format and obey the four-page maximum for each biographical sketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training entry
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING: Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, and include postdoctoral training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each entry list INSTITUTION AND LOCATION, DEGREE (if applicable), YEAR(s), and FIELD OF STUDY (e.g., Hendrix College, B.A., 1993, Biology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Positions and honors
rubrics_metrics.description: List professional positions (with dates) and honors for key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chronological positions with dates and concise honor listings (e.g., travel awards, grants). Use this section to show relevant experience and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected peer-reviewed publications (chronological)
rubrics_metrics.description: List selected peer-reviewed publications in chronological order for each key person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full citations (authors, year, title, journal, volume:pages). You may include manuscripts submitted or in preparation but distinguish their status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research support (Completed and Pending)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Completed Research Support and Pending Research Support entries for key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List grant number, funding institute, project title/short description, major goal, role (e.g., PI), and project dates (start–end). Separate completed from pending support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the facilities to be used for the conduct of the proposed research. Indicate the performance sites and describe capacities, pertinent capabilities, relative proximity, and extent of availability to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 'Other,' identify support services such as machine shop, electronics shop, and specify the extent to which they will be available to the project. Use continuation pages if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources inventory (Laboratory/Clinical/Animal/Computer/Office/Other)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe resources available to the project under headings such as Laboratory, Clinical, Animal, Computer, Office, and Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State lab square footage, proximity of PI/co-investigator labs, collective equipment availability, network and software access (e.g., connection to campus servers and software like GCG), and any shared/common facilities (dishwashing, water production). Note 'Not applicable' where appropriate (e.g., Clinical/Animal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Major equipment listing
rubrics_metrics.description: List the most important equipment items already available for this project, noting the location and pertinent capabilities of each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific (e.g., automated DNA sequencer ABI Model 377, oligonucleotide synthesizer Perceptive Expedite, high-speed and ultracentrifuges, biosafety hoods). Indicate where equipment is located and that common equipment areas include major equipment necessary to complete the experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: audience and background framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims should start with the background for the informed non-expert, writing at about the level of Scientific American.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a summary useful for non-primary reviewers and put less technical information first so reviewers from different backgrounds can quickly grasp the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: hypothesis presentation and health importance
rubrics_metrics.description: State the hypothesis so it is easy to locate (e.g., in bold) and include the health importance of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight the hypothesis (bolding recommended) and explicitly connect it to public health significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: justification of hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multiple reasons supporting the hypothesis with references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example provides three reasons for the hypothesis, each with citations; include supporting evidence and cite relevant literature (including key preliminary observations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: concise, limited scope and clear aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit scope to a small number of specific aims (example limits to three specific aims listed in bold) and follow each with a brief description of how the aim will be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List aims in bold with short descriptions/subsections for methods or approaches (e.g., A, B, C subsections outlining experiments and assays). This framing shows feasibility and a focused plan to test the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing style and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use short sentences, be neat, avoid typographical errors, and use bullets and numbered lists for effective organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use indents and bolding to add readability; lists act as guideposts for reviewers and help them scan and retrieve information quickly during review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Stay within the specified page limits for the application sections (example: stay within 25-page limit in original version prior to annotation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise and use continuation pages only where allowed. Overlength can hinder reviewer readability and violate application rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and significance: public health emphasis and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the importance of the research to public health in less technical terms that can be understood by all reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bolding to highlight key concepts so reviewers can scan quickly. Explain why the work matters clinically or for public health, and relate it to current unmet needs (e.g., antibiotic resistance, biofilm formation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of figures and illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use figures to illustrate points; figures can be essential to understanding transcripts, regulation, or proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include figures (with captions) that summarize or model key concepts (e.g., loci diagrams, regulatory models, schematic representations) to help reviewers grasp complex material at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of references and preliminary/unpublished data
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate broad understanding of the field using appropriate references, including preliminary and unpublished data where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite published work and relevant preliminary observations; use references to establish rationale, identify gaps, and support the experimental approach. Distinguish unpublished or personal communications as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim-level methods and feasibility statements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each aim, briefly describe the experimental approach and specific assays that will be used to accomplish the aim (e.g., Western blot, EMSA, DNA footprinting, transcriptional fusions, PCR-assisted binding site selection, computer-assisted alignments, Northern blot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough methodological detail to convince reviewers of feasibility without overwhelming with technical minutiae. Break aims into labeled subparts (A, B, C) with short method descriptions and expected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities/resources should demonstrate support for proposed methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities and shared resources in a way that confirms availability of space, equipment, common facility support, and technical services required by the proposed experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention proximity of PI and co-investigator labs, availability of high-quality water production, electronics shop, image documentation systems, and access to computing resources and specialized software to support data analysis.
